why: Midblock pedestrian crossing outside the marked crossing (WALK_X=122 m, hazard x=180-220 m). Speed 1.3-1.8 m/s lies within the FHWA walking range 0.8-1.8 m/s: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/publications/research/safety/04091/02.cfm . Trigger 44-56 m gives about 3.5-4.5 s at nominal ego speed 12.5 m/s, within the 3.2-6.28 s initial TTC range of observed mild deceleration interactions in Sun et al. (2022), Table 1; x varies +/-20 m around the selected midblock site: https://pureadmin.qub.ac.uk/ws/portalfiles/portal/388245508/sensors-22-07860.pdf . Exposure 0.02 per 0.2-km simulated street passage is an explicit proxy: that study screened 98 single-pedestrian non-intersection crossings from about 980 km of campus driving, so (98/980 km)*0.2 km = 0.02. It is not a measured jaywalking rate for this town; local crossing counts and trip lengths would be needed to calibrate it.
